questions.q: In which year was the first census of India conducted, and during whose tenure?
questions.explanation: The first census of India was conducted in 1872 during the time of Lord Mayo. Regular decennial census in India started in 1881 during the time of Lord Ripon.

questions.q: Regular (decennial) census in India started in which year, and under whose Viceroyalty?

questions.q: After the separation of Bihar from Odisha in 1936, in which year was the census of Bihar conducted separately for the first time?

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding rural and urban population of Bihar as per Census 2011:
1. The rural population percentage of Bihar (88.7%) is higher than the national average (68.8%).
2. The urban population percentage of Bihar (11.3%) is lower than the national average (31.2%).
3. The decadal growth rate of urbanisation in Bihar (0.8%) is lower than the national rate (3.4%).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Bihar is significantly more rural than the national average, has a much lower urban population share, and a much slower urbanisation growth rate than India as a whole.
questions.source: Self-authored, based on Eduteria Bihar Tathya Sangrah chapter content

questions.q: As per Census 2011, what was the child sex ratio (0-6 years) of Bihar compared to India?

options.A: Bihar 935; India 919 (Bihar higher than national average)
options.B: Bihar 919; India 935 (Bihar lower than national average)

questions.answer_text: Bihar 935; India 919 (Bihar higher than national average)
questions.explanation: Bihar's child sex ratio (935) as per Census 2011 was actually higher than the national average (919), even though its overall sex ratio (918) was lower than the national figure (943).
questions.source: Self-authored, based on Eduteria Bihar Tathya Sangrah chapter content

questions.q: According to Census 2011, what was the population density of Bihar compared to the national average?
questions.explanation: Bihar's population density (1106 persons per sq. km) as per Census 2011 was nearly three times the national average of 382 persons per sq. km, making it the most densely populated state.
questions.source: Self-authored, based on Eduteria Bihar Tathya Sangrah chapter content

questions.q: What was the growth in literacy rate in Bihar between the 2001 and 2011 census, compared to the national growth?
questions.explanation: Between 2001 and 2011, Bihar's literacy rate grew by 17.9 percentage points, a faster growth than the national average growth of 10.9 percentage points, though Bihar's absolute literacy rate remained below the national average.
questions.source: Self-authored, based on Eduteria Bihar Tathya Sangrah chapter content
